AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 31.08.2015 PASSED IN MVC NO. 60/2014 ON THE FILE OF THE II ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MEMBER ADDITIONAL MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL, HUBBALLI, AWARDING THE COMPENSATION OF RS.

These appeals are filed against the judgment and award dated 31.08.2015 in M.V.C.No.60/2014 on the file of II Additional Senior Civil Judge and AMACT, Hubballi.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Claimants are before this Court in M.F.A.No.101392/2016 not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation and for enhancement of compensation whereas insurer is before this Court in M.F.A.No.100313/2016 on the ground that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is exorbitant and on the ground that the claimants were not depended on the income of the deceased.

2. Brief facts of the case are that the claimants being the wife and daughter of the deceased Vijay Rao filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 claiming compensation for the accidental death of one Vijay Rao, husband of the first claimant in a road traffic accident that occurred on 26.09.2013 involving the motorcycle bearing No.KA-25/EL-0391.
It is submitted that the deceased was working as FDA in SDM Engineering and Technology College, Dharwad and was earning Rs.28,700/- p.m.

entities.text: SDM Engineering and Technology College, Dharwad
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is also stated that the deceased was aged 56 years as on the date of accident.
Respondent No.2 insurer, on service of notice, appeared before the Tribunal and filed objections denying the claim petition averments.

Further it is stated that the rider of the offending motorcycle had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
3. Claimant No.1 wife of the deceased examined herself as PW-1 and marked Exs.P-1 to P-8 whereas respondents marked Ex.R-1 copy of the policy.

Based on the material on record, the Tribunal awarded total compensation of Rs.15,77,793/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation under the following heads:
 Sl

sentences.text: While awarding the above compensation, the Tribunal assessed monthly income of the deceased at Rs.28,500/- after deducting professional tax of Rs.200/-, deducted 1/3rd towards personal expenses of the deceased and adopted split multiplier.
5. Learned counsel Sri G.N. Raichur for insurer would submit that the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side and prays for reduction of the same.
It is also contended that both the claimants i.e., wife and daughter of the deceased are working in postal department and bank respectively.
Therefore, they are not dependants of the deceased when they are earning, they cannot claim compensation on the head loss of dependency.

Learned counsel further submitted that PW-1 in her evidence admitted that she is working in postal department whereas daughter is working in bank and the Tribunal ignoring the evidence of PW-1 with regard to their employment, proceeded to award compensation on the head loss of dependency.
Thus, he prays for allowing the appeal filed by the insurance company.

6. Learned counsel Mrutyunjaya S. Hallikeri for claimants through video conference would submit that the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side and the Tribunal committed a grave error in adopting split multiplier while determining the compensation on the head loss of dependency.
Learned counsel would further submit that the claimants were depended on the income of the deceased as they were receiving meager salary working in postal department and bank.
There is no material whatsoever to contend that the claimants were not depended on the income of the deceased and he submits that on the other hand, claimants were dependent of deceased.
Thus, he would pray for allowing the appeal filed by the claimants and for enhancement of compensation.

7. On hearing the learned counsel for parties and on perusal of the records, the points that would arise for consideration are that 1) Whether the insurer is right in contending that the claimants were not depended on the income of the deceased?
2) Whether the Tribunal is justified in adopting split multiplier while determining the compensation on the head loss of dependency?
8. The answer to the above points is in the negative for the following reasons:
The accident that occurred on 26.09.2013 involving motorcycle bearing No.KA-25/EL-0391 and accidental death of Vijay Rao, husband of first claimant is not in dispute in these appeals.
Claimants are wife and daughter of the deceased.

Dharwad and was earning monthly salary of Rs.28,700/- which is evidenced by salary certificate at Ex.P-8.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Tribunal is justified in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs28,500/- p.m. after deducting Rs.200/- towards professional tax.

The main contention advanced by the learned counsel for insurer is that the Tribunal has committed error in awarding compensation under the head loss of dependency since the claimants are working in the postal department and bank respectively.

No doubt,
PW-1 in cross-examination stated that she is working in the postal department and second claimant is working in bank, but there is no evidence as to the earning of the claimants.
The respondent-insurer has not cross-examined as to, salary or income they were earning working in postal department and bank respectively.
No material is made available by the insurer or cross-examined with regard to their earning to determine their dependency on the deceased.

As there is no material evidence and the claim petition is filed stating that the husband was only earning member in the family, the Tribunal has proceeded to grant compensation on the head loss of dependency.
Mere admission that claimants are working would not mean that they were not dependent on the deceased.
Therefore, there is no merit in the contention of the insurer that claimants were not entitled for compensation on the head loss of dependency.
9. As contented by the claimants, the Tribunal has committed error in adopting split multiplier while determining the compensation under the head loss of dependency.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of R Valli vs. Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation Ltd.,1 has made it clear that the method of determination of compensation applying two multipliers is clearly erroneous and run counter to the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others2.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since deceased was aged 50 years, multiplier 9 is to be applied.

Thus, the claimants are entitled for the compensation towards loss of dependency as under:
Rs.28,500 + 10%= Rs.31,350/-
Rs.31,350 - 10,450 (1/3rd of Rs.31,350/-) = Rs.20,900/- Rs.20,900 x 12 x 9 =
Rs.22,57,200/-
10.
The Tribunal has also committed grave error in awarding Rs.1,00,000/- on the head loss of consortium and Rs.25,000/- towards funeral expenses.

In terms of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs Nanu Ram 3, first claimant would be entitled for a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of spousal consortium and second claimant 2022 8 SCC 107 (2017) 16 SCC 680 (2018) SCC 130 - 10 - would be entitled for Rs.40,000/- on the head loss of parental consortium.

- 11 - ORDER i) M.F.A.No.101392/2016 filed by the claimants is allowed in part.
ii) M.F.A.No.100313/2016 filed by the insurance company is dismissed.

iii) The judgment and award dated 31.08.2015 in M.V.C.No.60/2014 on the file of II Additional Senior Civil Judge and AMACT, Hubballi is modified and the appellant/claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.8,36,016/- at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation excluding the interest on the enhanced compensation for the delayed period of 144 days.
iv) The insurance company shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment excluding the interest on the enhanced compensation for the delayed period of 144 days.
v) Apportionment, deposit and disbursement of the enhanced compensation shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.
vi) Draw modified award accordingly.

The medical expenses awarded by the Tribunal in a sum of Rs.46,609/- is not disturbed.
